1606.04474.tldr: The original proof that an optimization procedure can itself be learned. An LSTM is trained to act as an optimizer — ingesting gradients and emitting weight updates — by unrolling the optimizee's training.
results: The learned optimizer generalizes to optimizees, networks, and task distributions it was not trained on.
Recovered hand-designed behavior (momentum-style updates) without being told to.
limitations: Meta-trained on small, specific task distributions; scaling to large-scale training remained open (and largely still is).
1606.04474.fits: The conceptual root of the whole list: if the *improver* is learnable, then the improver can be improved. Everything from TextGrad to DGM is a descendant of this idea.
1606.04474.reading: Read §2–3 (the coordinatewise LSTM and how unrolling works); skim the transfer experiments.

2410.04444.tldr: The self-referential ideal made concrete with an LLM: the agent's behavior is code (prompts + tools) that it can inspect and rewrite, so no fixed, hand-designed optimizer sits in the loop.
results: The agent can modify its own logic and improve without a human-authored optimization routine.
Demonstrates self-reference and code-as-identity as an RSI substrate.
limitations: Self-modification is bounded and validated heuristically — no formal guarantees of goal preservation.
2410.04444.fits: The theory-side counterpart to the empirical Darwin Gödel Machine (stage 7). Read them as a pair: this is the 'what', DGM is the 'does it work'.
2410.04444.reading: Focus on how it frames self-reference (§3) and the self-modification loop; the paper is more a framework than a benchmark result.

2003.03384.tldr: Evolves complete ML algorithms — not just hyperparameters — from a tiny space of scalar/vector math operations, discovering update rules that work from scratch.
results: Rediscovered backpropagation and Adam-style momentum purely through evolution.
Evolved algorithms that generalize to held-out tasks, with minimal human bias in the search space.
limitations: Only tiny problems (small MLPs, toy datasets); doesn't scale to modern models.
2003.03384.fits: Pre-LLM 'AI designing AI'. The evolutionary-search machinery here is the direct ancestor of AlphaEvolve and MLEvolve (stage 9 / stage 8).
2003.03384.reading: Skim the search-space design (§3) and the discovered algorithms (§4); don't dwell on the experimental scale.

2310.03714.tldr: Reframes prompt engineering as program optimization: declare what each LM call does (a signature), then let a compiler optimize the prompts and few-shot demos inside against a metric.
results: GPT-3.5 + DSPy pipelines matched or beat hand-written GPT-4 prompts on several tasks.
The optimizer (bootstrapped demos or a prompted optimizer) is reusable across tasks.
limitations: Needs a well-defined automatic metric — the optimization is only as good as that signal.
Prompt/compile quality still depends on the underlying search or bootstrap strategy.
2310.03714.fits: The most *useful* artifact in the list: it's the mental model (separate structure from parameters) that harness-level RSI generalizes. Read before TextGrad.
2310.03714.reading: Read the signature/module abstractions (§2–3) and one optimizer (§4). Then actually try the library.

2406.07496.tldr: Generalizes backprop to text: treat every textual variable in a compound system as a parameter, and backpropagate natural-language criticism through the graph to update each one.
results: Optimizes prompts, code, and answers in one end-to-end loop.
Outperformed hand-crafted prompts and prior prompt optimizers across reasoning and coding benchmarks.
limitations: Textual 'gradients' can be noisy or uninformative; performance is still bounded by the base model's capability.
2406.07496.fits: The cleanest mental model of 'differentiating' an AI pipeline. Pair with DSPy: DSPy is structured program optimization, TextGrad is free-form textual backprop.
2406.07496.reading: Read the computation-graph formalism (§3) and the text-gradient update rule (§4).

2303.11366.tldr: Verbal reinforcement learning: when the agent fails, it writes a natural-language reflection on what went wrong, stores it in memory, and injects it into the next attempt — no weight updates.
results: 91% pass@1 on HumanEval with GPT-4, a large jump over the base model.
Improved on decision-making (AlfWorld) and sequential reasoning without any fine-tuning.
limitations: Improvement lives only in the context window — bounded and non-persistent across sessions.
Works best on episodic tasks with clear success/failure signals.
2303.11366.fits: The ancestor of nearly every 'memory agent' in stage 4 (ExpeL, A-MEM, EvolveR, …). Read it first and watch how each successor adds persistence or structure.
2303.11366.reading: Read §3 (the reflect→store→retry loop) and the HumanEval result. Short paper.

2305.16291.tldr: Lifelong skill acquisition in Minecraft: an automatic curriculum proposes tasks, execution-verified code skills accumulate in a library, and feedback refines them — all with a frozen GPT-4.
results: ~3.3× more unique items collected and key tech-tree milestones unlocked far faster than prior agents.
The skill library compounds: later tasks reuse and build on earlier verified skills.
limitations: Minecraft-specific and depends on a strong base model; skill code can still hallucinate and needs environment feedback to correct.
2305.16291.fits: The canonical *skill-library* paradigm. Its 'code-as-skill, verify-in-environment' loop is reused by DGM, AgentFactory, and the embodied self-improvement line.
2305.16291.reading: Read the three components (§3–4) and the automatic-curriculum mechanism; then run the repo (stage 10).

2510.04618.tldr: Treats context as an evolving 'playbook' that accumulates and organizes strategies via generation, reflection, and curation — using structured incremental edits to avoid context collapse.
results: +10.6% over strong baselines on agent benchmarks and +8.6% on finance/domain tasks.
Works both offline (system prompts) and online (agent memory), scaling with long-context models.
limitations: Still bounded by context capacity; the brevity-bias vs. detail tradeoff is managed, not eliminated.
2510.04618.fits: The 'evolve the whole context, not just a skill' generalization of stage 4. Contrasts with Voyager (which evolves *code skills*) by evolving the *prompt/context itself*.
2510.04618.reading: Read the generation/reflection/curation loop (§3) and how incremental updates prevent collapse.

2510.16079.tldr: A closed-loop experience lifecycle: trajectories are distilled into a repository of abstract 'strategic principles', retrieved at task time, and the policy is reinforced from outcomes.
results: Outperforms baselines by refining *strategy* (not just factual memory) across agent tasks.
The offline-distillation + online-retrieval split makes learning persistent and reusable.
limitations: Distillation quality depends on trajectory coverage; retrieval can surface irrelevant principles.
2510.16079.fits: The cleanest end-to-end 'experience → principle → policy' loop in stage 4. A direct, structured successor to Reflexion.
2510.16079.reading: Read the two-stage lifecycle (§3) and how principles are distilled and retrieved.

2605.23904.tldr: Trains the skill document as the external state of a frozen agent, with a separate optimizer model making bounded add/delete/replace edits accepted only on held-out validation gain.
results: Improves across six benchmarks, seven target models, and three execution harnesses.
Zero extra inference-time model calls at deployment — all optimization happens offline.
limitations: Bounded, acceptance-gated edits are deliberately conservative — the tradeoff is a slower skill-evolution rate.
2605.23904.fits: The 'treat the skill like a trained parameter' position — skill evolution with the discipline of weight-space optimization. Contrasts with free-form self-revision approaches.
2605.23904.reading: Read the textual-learning-rate / acceptance-gate design (§3–4) — that discipline is the reusable idea.

2408.08435.tldr: A meta-agent programs new agents: it proposes agent designs as executable code, evaluates them, and iterates — including a re-architect step that learns to improve the meta-agent's own prompt.
results: Discovered agents that outperform state-of-the-art hand-designed agents on coding, math, and QA benchmarks.
Agents transfer across models (e.g., discovered agents boost GPT-4 performance).
limitations: Search is compute-hungry (many LLM calls); the meta-agent itself is initially hand-designed.
2408.08435.fits: The harness-level flagship: the 'improver' is an agent generating executable improvements. Stage 5's anchor — most later harness-evolution work extends this loop.
2408.08435.reading: Read the meta-agent search + re-architect mechanism (§3) and the transfer results.

2310.02304.tldr: Bootstraps a recursive code improver from a seed: an LLM writes and improves a scaffolding program, and that generated program is itself an improver that can improve the code that improves it.
results: Improved over GPT-4 on GSM8K and WebShop, including the generated improver improving itself.
Demonstrates the improver-improves-the-improver loop on real code.
limitations: Recursive gains can plateau; depends on a strong seed model and self-improvement meta-prompt.
2310.02304.fits: The most literal 'recursive' demo — the scaffolding that does the improving is itself improved. A bridge between ADAS (search) and DGM (self-modification).
2310.02304.reading: Read the seed-improver construction and the meta-prompt (§3–4). Short paper.

2605.09998.tldr: Reset-free online self-improvement for embodied agents: the agent alternates between acting and refining its own prompt, sub-agents, skills, and memory within one continuous trajectory.
results: Originated from Gemini Plays Pokémon — the first system to complete Pokémon Blue/Yellow Legacy (hard mode) and Crystal without a lost battle.
Removes the human from the refinement loop, automating what was previously human-in-the-loop harness tuning.
limitations: Embodied/eval cost is high; single-trajectory online adaptation is complex to stabilize.
2605.09998.fits: The embodied, reset-free counterpart to prompt-optimization harnesses. Extends the loop toward model-weight co-learning — a bridge to SIA's joint updates.
2605.09998.reading: Read the act/refine alternation (§3) and the Pokémon results; note the contrast with reset-based prompt optimizers.

2605.27276.tldr: A single Feedback-Agent updates both the harness and the weights of a task agent, unifying the two previously siloed self-improvement schools (harness-update vs. test-time training).
results: Improves across three contrasting domains (e.g., Chinese legal charge classification and low-level coding).
Shows joint harness+weight updates beat updating either one in isolation.
limitations: Two-module complexity; evaluations are domain-specific rather than a single unified benchmark.
2605.27276.fits: The 'close the loop' paper — harness-level and model-level RSI are not separate; this merges them. Read after Continual Harness.
2605.27276.reading: Read the Feedback-Agent architecture (§3) and how harness and weight updates are coordinated.

2505.15734.tldr: Ground-truth-free self-training: generate multi-agent debate traces (with a Reflect-Critique-Refine prompt), fine-tune on the model's own improved traces, and repeat.
results: +8.92% on GSM-PLUS and ~+5.8% average across six other reasoning benchmarks.
Cross-domain generalization suggests it captures general reasoning, not task overfitting.
limitations: Debate quality ceilings the improvement; requires multiple forward passes per sample during trace generation.
2505.15734.fits: Closes the loop that inference-time debate (stage 6) leaves open — it *persists* debate gains into weights, with no labels.
2505.15734.reading: Read the Reflect-Critique-Refine strategy (§3) and the debate→train loop (§4).

2505.22954.tldr: The flagship empirical self-modifier: a coding agent edits its own source code, keeps only empirically-validated improvements, and archives them open-endedly.
results: Self-modification with archive-based evolution lets the agent improve the very code that runs its improvement loop.
Demonstrates compounding improvement over hand-crafted coding agents on coding tasks.
limitations: Validation is bounded by eval budget; self-edits can introduce bugs that must be caught by the evaluator.
2505.22954.fits: The 'does it actually work' answer to the Gödel Agent's 'what'. The Sakana blog is the best companion read. Run the repo (stage 10).
2505.22954.reading: Read the self-modification + validation loop (§3) and the archive (MAP-Elites-style) design (§4).

2504.15228.tldr: Minimal and transparent self-improvement: an agent with basic coding tools edits its own implementation, re-evaluates on benchmarks, and keeps only edits that help.
results: Gains from 17% to 53% on a random SWE-bench Verified subset, plus LiveCodeBench.
A data-efficient, non-gradient learning mechanism driven by reflection + code edits.
limitations: Evaluated on a random subset; gains can plateau as the agent exhausts easy self-edits.
2504.15228.fits: The simplest, most reproducible self-modifying agent — a great first read before DGM, which adds open-ended archives on top.
2504.15228.reading: Read the edit→evaluate→keep loop (§3) and the benchmark setup. Very short and concrete.

2408.06292.tldr: The first end-to-end ML research loop: generate ideas (novelty-checked), run experiments, plot and analyze, write a LaTeX paper, and score it with an automated reviewer — then iterate.
results: Produces complete papers at ~$15 each, with some results later independently reproduced/validated.
A fully reusable idea→paper→review loop for machine-learning research.
limitations: No vision experiments; occasionally mismatches idea and paper; the automated reviewer is weaker than human review; can hallucinate in the manuscript.
2408.06292.fits: The concrete 'AI doing AI research' baseline. v2 (stage 8) removes the template and adds agentic search; read both.
2408.06292.reading: Read the pipeline (§3) and the honest limitations (§6) — the limitations are as instructive as the method.

nature-ai-scientist-v2-2026.tldr: Automates the entire research cycle — ideas, code, experiments, plots, manuscript, and peer review — end to end, in focused (template-scaffolded) and template-free open-ended (agentic tree search) modes.
results: Its generated manuscript passed first-round peer review at a top-tier ML workshop (70% acceptance rate).
Template-free agentic search expands exploration beyond human-provided scaffolds.
limitations: Still confined to machine-learning research; workshop peer review is not full top-conference review.
nature-ai-scientist-v2-2026.fits: The peer-reviewed milestone that moves automated research from demo to capability. Compare its gains over v1 to see what 'removing the template' buys.
nature-ai-scientist-v2-2026.reading: Read the two modes (§2–3) and the peer-review outcome; contrast with v1's limitations.

nature-funsearch-2024.tldr: A frozen LLM proposes candidate functions in a problem skeleton; a separate evaluator scores them; the best are fed back as few-shot examples — an evolutionary loop that found new mathematics.
results: Discovered new cap-set constructions (size 512 in dimension 8) — the first progress on the problem in years.
Also found an improved online bin-packing heuristic.
limitations: Needs a clean, fast evaluator; only works for problems expressible as program search.
nature-funsearch-2024.fits: The clearest proof that LLM + evaluator + evolution can produce *novel* results humans hadn't found. The model/evaluator split is the key lesson AlphaEvolve scales up.
nature-funsearch-2024.reading: Read the evaluate→select→prompt loop (§2–3) and the cap-set result. The DeepMind blog is a good companion.

2506.13131.tldr: A Gemini-powered coding agent that generates candidate algorithms, evaluates them (often with fast approximate evaluators over a distributed pool), and improves them via island-based evolutionary search.
results: Discovered a faster 4×4 matrix-multiplication algorithm (fewer multiplications than prior best) and improved kernels.
Improvements include components used to train AI systems — the stack improving the stack.
limitations: Depends on fast/approximate evaluators; specialized to algorithmic kernels rather than general code.
2506.13131.fits: FunSearch at industrial scale, aimed at *practical* algorithmic kernels. The most direct modern instance of 'AI improving the AI training stack'.
2506.13131.reading: Read the evaluator-guided evolution loop (§3) and the matrix-multiplication case; pair with the DeepMind blog.

1905.10985.tldr: Clune's agenda paper: instead of hand-designing intelligence piece by piece, treat the *learning algorithm itself* as the thing to be searched for.
1905.10985.method: Position paper: proposes three pillars for producing general AI — meta-learn the architecture, meta-learn the algorithm (evolve/search over learning algorithms), and meta-learn the environments — so the AI-generating algorithm (AI-GA) does the search, not humans.
results: Formalizes the 'AI-generating algorithm' thesis: learning is the search target, not the artifact.
Articulates the safety argument that AI-GAs avoid hand-designing intelligence and can be bounded by design.
limitations: Conceptual only — no working system; all three pillars remain open research programs.
1905.10985.fits: The philosophical blueprint for this entire list — nearly every later entry instantiates one of Clune's pillars (AutoML-Zero = pillar 2, POET = pillar 3).
1905.10985.reading: Read the three pillars (§2–4); it's short and defines the vocabulary the rest of the list uses.

frontiers-quality-diversity-2016.tldr: The survey that named 'Quality Diversity': optimize for a *collection* of diverse, high-performing solutions rather than a single optimum.
frontiers-quality-diversity-2016.method: Survey/position: QD algorithms return an archive of solutions indexed by a behavior/feature descriptor, seeking to illuminate the whole search space (diversity) while maximizing each niche's quality.
results: Defines the illumination objective — diversity + quality — as a distinct alternative to pure optimization.
Frames MAP-Elites, Novelty Search, and their hybrids as one family under a shared lens.
limitations: Survey, no new algorithm; the difficulty of choosing a meaningful behavior characterization is left open.
frontiers-quality-diversity-2016.fits: Why DGM and AlphaEvolve keep *archives* instead of one best answer — the QD objective is the substrate that lets self-improvement explore without collapsing.
frontiers-quality-diversity-2016.reading: Read the illumination framing (§2) and the MAP-Elites description; skim the taxonomy.

1504.04909.tldr: MAP-Elites: keep the best solution found in every cell of a behavior grid, illuminating the space of possible high-quality designs.
1504.04909.method: Map each individual to a low-dimensional behavior/feature descriptor; maintain a grid where each cell stores the best-performing solution for that niche (elitism); keep perturbing elites to fill and improve cells.
results: Illuminates search spaces (e.g., 6-legged robot gaits) where a single optimum hides useful alternatives.
Elite diversity provides robustness and reusable stepping stones for later search.
limitations: Needs a cheap, meaningful descriptor; scales poorly as descriptor dimensionality grows.
1504.04909.fits: The specific QD algorithm reused by DGM's archive — 'keep the best of every niche' is what lets open-ended self-improvement explore without collapse.
1504.04909.reading: Read the algorithm box (§3) and the gait experiments; the mechanism matters more than the domain.

1112.5309.tldr: POWERPLAY: continually invent the simplest problem you can't yet solve, learn it, and freeze the skill — growing a general solver from scratch.
1112.5309.method: Two coupled searches: one finds new tasks the current solver can't do (the 'simplest still unsolvable' problem), the other trains the solver to master them; each learned skill is added and frozen so later learning doesn't destroy it.
results: Demonstrates unsupervised task invention that grows capability without a predefined curriculum.
Frozen, reusable skills prevent catastrophic forgetting as new abilities accumulate.
limitations: Tiny hand-crafted domains; the 'simplest still unsolvable' criterion is hard to scale to real tasks.
1112.5309.fits: The earliest 'generate your own curriculum' loop — POET (stage 9) is its modern, evolutionary descendant.
1112.5309.reading: Read the two coupled search processes (§3); skim the experiments.

2309.03409.tldr: OPRO: use the LLM itself as the optimizer — feed it scored solution history and ask for better candidates, in natural language.
2309.03409.method: Prompt the LLM with the optimization problem plus a sorted history of (solution, score) pairs; it proposes new candidate solutions (prompts); evaluate them and repeat the loop.
results: Discovers novel, sometimes human-unreadable prompts (like 'Take a deep breath') that beat hand-designed prompts on GSM8K and Big-Bench Hard.
limitations: Optimization is meta-prompt/temperature sensitive; needs a reliable scalar score signal.
2309.03409.fits: The simplest 'LLM as optimizer' loop — the prompt becomes the search space. Ancestor of Promptbreeder and the whole optimization-as-language arc.
2309.03409.reading: Read the meta-prompt design (§3) and the discovered-prompts results (§5).

2309.16797.tldr: Promptbreeder: evolve a *population* of prompts — and evolve the mutation prompts too, making the self-improvement self-referential.
2309.16797.method: Maintain a population of task prompts plus 'mutation prompts' (thinking styles); an LLM mutates prompts, evaluates fitness on a training set, and the mutation-prompt level is itself evolved — a two-level self-improvement loop.
results: Evolved prompts outperform strong hand-crafted baselines on arithmetic, commonsense, and ethics benchmarks.
limitations: Expensive (many evaluations); fitness is domain-specific and can overfit the training set.
2309.16797.fits: The self-referential version of OPRO: it evolves not just prompts but the *mutator* of prompts.
2309.16797.reading: Read the population + self-referential mutation design (§3); skim results.

2310.04406.tldr: LATS: wrap a frozen LM in Monte Carlo Tree Search — the model acts, an LM value function scores, and reflection on failures backpropagates learning.
2310.04406.method: MCTS where the LM proposes actions, an LM-trained value function scores states, the environment returns rewards, and reflection on failed trajectories is injected back into search.
results: State-of-the-art at the time on HumanEval, HotpotQA, and WebShop among reasoning/agent frameworks.
limitations: High inference cost (tree search); needs an environment or reliable reward for the search to work.
2310.04406.fits: Shows a frozen model can be improved by the *scaffold* (search), not its weights — a core harness-RSI motif.
2310.04406.reading: Read the MCTS integration (§3) and how reflection feeds search (§4).

2303.17651.tldr: Self-Refine: the same model generates, critiques its own output, and refines — the minimal self-improvement loop.
2303.17651.method: Iterate: generate an output, have the *same* model critique it, refine based on that feedback, and repeat until a stop condition — no training, no extra data.
results: Improves across 7 tasks (dialogue, code, math, …) with no training or extra data, in just a few iterations.
limitations: Feedback quality is bounded by the model itself; can loop without converging (see 'Cannot Self-Correct').
2303.17651.fits: The minimal self-improvement loop — one model as both solver and critic. Most stage-3/4 work refines this.
2303.17651.reading: Read the feedback/refine loop (§2) and the ablation on feedback quality (§5).

2309.11495.tldr: Chain-of-Verification: draft, then plan *independent* verification questions, answer them in isolation, and produce a fact-checked final answer.
2309.11495.method: Four steps: draft a response; generate verification questions; answer each independently (to avoid bias from the draft); produce a final response conditioned on the verified facts.
results: Reduces hallucination on factoid QA (e.g., Wikidata) with no external tools or retraining.
limitations: Only covers facts the model can self-check; independent answers still draw from the same model.
2309.11495.fits: Verification-as-scaffold: decompose the check so the model can't just confirm its own error.
2309.11495.reading: Read the four-step pipeline (§3); note why 'independent answering' is the key design choice.

2305.11738.tldr: CRITIC: self-correction with *external tools* — search, an interpreter, and other tools gather corrective evidence before revising.
2305.11738.method: Generate → ask the model to critique its own output → use external tools (web search, code interpreter, etc.) to gather corrective evidence → revise against that grounded feedback.
results: Improves factuality (with search), code execution (with interpreter), and safety across several benchmarks.
limitations: Depends on tool availability/quality; still bounded by the model's revision ability.
2305.11738.fits: Adds *grounded* feedback to Self-Refine — the correction loop touches the real world instead of only self-assessing.
2305.11738.reading: Read the tool-interactive critique loop (§3) and one tool's results (§4).

2203.11171.tldr: Self-Consistency: sample many chain-of-thought paths and take the majority answer — reliability through diversity, not refinement.
2203.11171.method: Sample a diverse set of reasoning paths (instead of greedy decoding), then select the most consistent final answer by marginalizing over the sampled paths (majority vote).
results: Large accuracy gains over greedy decoding on arithmetic and commonsense reasoning, with no extra training.
limitations: Pure inference-time ensemble — multiplies compute and only helps when errors are independent.
2203.11171.fits: The 'variance reduction' cousin of self-improvement; complements Self-Refine (diversity vs. refinement).
2203.11171.reading: Read the sampling/marginalization idea (§3); the mechanism is one short section.

2305.20050.tldr: Let's Verify Step by Step: reward *each reasoning step* (process supervision), not just the final answer — and show it beats outcome supervision.
2305.20050.method: Train a reward model with process supervision — feedback on every intermediate step, not just the final result — and use it to rank/generate solutions; active learning picks which steps to label.
results: Process-supervised RM solves 78.2% of MATH vs. 72.4% for outcome supervision; step-level active learning is notably data-efficient.
limitations: Requires expensive step-level human labels; the PRM is itself a large trained model.
2305.20050.fits: Shows *where* feedback is placed changes what a self-improving system learns — the verification layer is itself trainable.
2305.20050.reading: Read the process vs. outcome supervision contrast (§2–3) and the MATH result.

2310.01798.tldr: The counterweight: LLMs often *can't* reliably self-correct their own reasoning without external feedback — and trying can make them worse.
2310.01798.method: Systematic measurement: test whether intrinsic self-correction helps; show that when the model can't detect its own errors, self-correction frequently degrades accuracy relative to the initial answer.
results: Intrinsic self-correction often hurts; reliable gains appear only with external feedback or ground-truth signals.
limitations: A cautionary measurement paper, not a method; conclusions reflect then-current models.
2310.01798.fits: The essential check on the whole stage-3 arc — self-correction is not free. Read it to know *when* loops help vs. hurt.
2310.01798.reading: Read the experiments contrasting intrinsic vs. extrinsic feedback (§4).

2308.10144.tldr: ExpeL: distill successful trajectories into an insight rule-base, reflect on failures to revise it, and retrieve insights at inference — no weight updates.
2308.10144.method: Two phases: (1) gather successful trajectories and extract natural-language insights; (2) on failure, reflect and update the insight base — then retrieve relevant insights to guide future attempts.
results: Consistent gains on HotpotQA and ALFWorld vs. strong baselines (e.g., Reflexion), including transfer of insights across similar tasks.
limitations: Extraction/retrieval quality is the bottleneck; open-ended but bounded by the insight bank.
2308.10144.fits: The 'distill trajectories into a rule base' memory agent — bridges Reflexion's episodic memory toward persistent, transferable principles.
2308.10144.reading: Read the insight extraction + success/failure split (§3); note the transfer experiment.

2502.12110.tldr: A-MEM: memory as a Zettelkasten-style linked graph that *reorganizes itself* — an agentic memory system, not a fixed store.
2502.12110.method: Structures memories as linked notes with context and timestamps; a memory agent dynamically creates, links, and updates memories from new dialogs, so organization evolves with experience.
results: Improves recall and downstream QA on LoCoMo and other long-context memory benchmarks over fixed-structure memory.
limitations: Graph organization depends on the memory agent's decisions; retrieval can still surface irrelevant nodes.
2502.12110.fits: Memory that reorganizes itself — the memory system is an agent. Sets up the 'evolve the memory' line (MemEvolve).
2502.12110.reading: Read the memory formation + evolution loops (§3–4) and the LoCoMo results.

2305.10250.tldr: MemoryBank: long-term memory for companions — summarize events and apply an Ebbinghaus forgetting curve for consistent, long-horizon recall.
2305.10250.method: Maintain a long-term memory bank of summarized past events with an Ebbinghaus-inspired decay; retrieve relevant memories so multi-day companion/counseling interactions stay consistent beyond the context window.
results: Enables consistent multi-day companion interactions (persona and history recall) beyond context limits.
limitations: Domain-specific (companion/counseling); summary-based storage loses detail.
2305.10250.fits: The 'memory as database with decay' baseline — contrast with agentic memory (A-MEM) and evolving memory (MemEvolve).
2305.10250.reading: Read the memory bank + forgetting-curve design (§3).

2604.15097.tldr: Strategy Genes: skill *documents* are unstable control; compact 'strategy genes' (skill IDs + parameters) control and evolve more reliably.
2604.15097.method: 4.6k controlled trials across 45 code scenarios: compare documentation-oriented skill packages vs. compact 'strategy genes' (skill identifiers + config); show compact, stable representations control and evolve better.
results: Expanding compact experience into fuller docs often fails to help and can degrade average performance.
Compact strategy genes give stabler test-time control and a cleaner substrate for iterative evolution.
limitations: Beta technical report; results are specific to code-solving scenarios.
2604.15097.fits: A warning for the skill-library paradigm (Voyager/ACE): bigger skill docs ≠ better control. The 'gene' framing links memory evolution to evolutionary RSI.
2604.15097.reading: Read the skill-package vs. strategy-gene comparison (§3) and the controlled-trial design.

2602.07755.tldr: ALMA: meta-learn the memory *design* itself — learning to continually learn, instead of hand-crafting a fixed memory.
2602.07755.method: Instead of a hand-crafted fixed memory, meta-learn the memory design (what to store, how to update/retrieve) so it adapts to task diversity and non-stationarity — learning-to-continually-learn.
results: Outperforms fixed, human-designed memory on continual-learning/adaptation tasks.
limitations: Meta-learning adds a training loop; learned memory designs are task-distribution-specific.
2602.07755.fits: Memory whose *architecture* is learned, not engineered — the same target MemEvolve reaches via evolution, here via meta-learning.
2602.07755.reading: Read the meta-learning-over-memory formulation (§3) and how it differs from fixed memory.

2607.14159.tldr: MemoHarness: optimize the whole agent *harness* (context, tools, orchestration, memory, decoding) — and learn it from the agent's own executions.
2607.14159.method: Frames the harness as the optimization target; MemoHarness learns harness policies from its own execution traces rather than optimizing a single narrow artifact like a prompt.
results: Adaptive per-case harnesses improve agent behavior vs. a single global harness.
limitations: Large harness search space; needs execution feedback to attribute harness edits to outcomes.
2607.14159.fits: Expands the self-improvement target from prompts/pipelines to the *whole harness* — the bridge from stage-4 memory to stage-5 harness evolution.
2607.14159.reading: Read how harness components are parameterized and learned (§3–4).

2607.26784.tldr: SkillRise: learn reusable skills *across* related tasks with a unified RL objective and progressive curricula — not per-task retries.
2607.26784.method: Unified RL framework that groups related task instances into progressive curricula and learns transferable skills across tasks, replacing per-task RL and multi-stage extraction/retrieval/execution pipelines.
results: Cross-task skill learning outperforms per-task RL and pipeline-based skill baselines.
limitations: Requires tasks that genuinely share solution patterns; RL sample cost.
2607.26784.fits: Unifies skill acquisition with RL so skills transfer — closing the gap between Voyager-style skill libraries and agentic RL.
2607.26784.reading: Read the curriculum grouping + unified RL objective (§3–4).

2512.18746.tldr: MemEvolve: evolve the memory *system itself* — its storage, distillation, and tool synthesis — not just its contents.
2512.18746.method: Treat the memory architecture (storage, distillation, tool synthesis) as the evolving object: an outer evolutionary loop mutates and selects memory-system designs, removing the 'static memory' bottleneck.
results: Evolving the memory system yields gains over manually engineered memory across agent tasks.
limitations: Evolutionary search over memory architectures is expensive; gains are environment-dependent.
2512.18746.fits: The 'evolve the memory, not just use it' position — one level above agent-level evolution. Pairs with ALMA as two routes to the same target.
2512.18746.reading: Read how the memory-system space is encoded and evolved (§3–4).

2607.05297.tldr: MetaSkill-Evolve: recursive skill improvement — a fast loop rewrites task skills, a slow loop evolves the meta-skill that improves skills.
2607.05297.method: Two-timescale loop: a fast loop rewrites task skills from execution traces; a slow loop evolves the meta-skill (the skill that improves skills), making self-improvement recursive rather than one-level.
results: Recursive improvement of the skill-improver yields gains beyond non-recursive skill rewriting.
limitations: Two-timescale stability is tricky; recursive gain can plateau.
2607.05297.fits: Makes skill evolution actually *recursive* — the improver is itself improved, the definitional move of RSI applied to skills.
2607.05297.reading: Read the two-timescale separation (§3) and how the meta-skill is updated.

2604.25850.tldr: Agentic Harness Engineering: automate harness evolution by instrumenting three things — components, trajectories, and edit attribution.
2604.25850.method: Closed loop over three observability pillars: (1) component observability (track each harness component), (2) trajectory observability (surface actionable signal in long traces), (3) attribution (link edits to effects) — to automate harness editing for coding agents.
results: Automatic harness evolution improves coding-agent performance where manual harness tuning was the bottleneck.
limitations: Observability infrastructure is heavy; attribution of edits remains approximate.
2604.25850.fits: Turns harness engineering from manual craft into a measurable, closed-loop process — the instrumentation prerequisite for all stage-5 harness evolution.
2604.25850.reading: Read the three observability pillars (§3) and the attribution mechanism (§4).

2608.12307.tldr: AI4AI at Test-Time: a strong builder model constructs inference-time harnesses that help a *weaker* model — strong-to-weak transfer with no weight updates.
2608.12307.method: A strong builder model constructs inference-time harnesses/scaffolds that let a weaker target model solve tasks more reliably — strong-to-weak distillation, but at test time with no parameter updates.
results: Builder-constructed harnesses improve weak-model reliability across four representative Theory-of-Mind benchmarks.
limitations: Transfer is bounded by what the harness can express; no durable gain (the weak model is unchanged).
2608.12307.fits: Harness as a *transfer* channel: the improving intelligence lives in the scaffold, not the weights — a clean contrast to SIA's joint weight updates.
2608.12307.reading: Read the strong-to-weak scaffolding setup (§3) and the four-benchmark results.

2603.03329.tldr: AutoHarness: automatically synthesize a code harness of guards so the agent can't take illegal actions (like the illegal chess moves behind 78% of Gemini losses).
2603.03329.method: The LLM synthesizes a code harness around the agent — a guard layer that wraps raw actions so illegal ones are caught or blocked before execution.
results: Auto-synthesized harnesses eliminate illegal-move failures and improve agent reliability.
limitations: Covers only actions anticipated at synthesis time; needs re-synthesis as the domain shifts.
2603.03329.fits: The 'safety-rail as harness' perspective — self-improvement by constraining the action space, complementing the exploration-focused harness work.
2603.03329.reading: Read the harness-synthesis loop (§3) and the chess case study.

2608.05446.tldr: EvoHarness-RL: learn the runtime harness with RL — forming state from noisy traces and controlling access to external state.
2608.05446.method: RL trains a runtime harness to (1) form state from noisy interaction traces and (2) control access to external state, replacing prompt/heuristic/convention-based workspace management.
results: Learned harness state + policy improves long-horizon agent execution over hand-crafted conventions.
limitations: RL over harness actions needs a task-outcome reward; state formation from noisy traces is hard.
2608.05446.fits: Harness evolution *as reinforcement learning* — the workspace and its policy are learned, not engineered.

2603.19461.tldr: Hyperagents: the meta-level mechanism that improves the agent is itself code, so it too can be improved — self-improvement without a fixed handcrafted meta-layer.
2603.19461.method: Builds on the Darwin Gödel Machine: since evaluation and self-modification are both coding tasks, the meta-level (the improvement mechanism) is coded and improvable — hyperagents improve their own improvement.
results: Demonstrates improvable meta-levels, removing the fixed handcrafted meta-mechanism that bounds ordinary self-improvement.
limitations: Framework + coding-domain bound; open-ended meta-improvement is hard to validate.
2603.19461.fits: The deepest step on the self-improvement ladder — not just improving the agent, but improving the *improver*. Read after DGM.
2603.19461.reading: Read the meta-level vs. object-level framing (§2–3) and the DGM relationship.

2603.18000.tldr: AgentFactory: store successful solutions as executable *subagent code* (not text reflections), refined by execution feedback and reused as building blocks.
2603.18000.method: Self-evolution that preserves successful task solutions as executable subagent code; subagents are continuously refined from execution feedback and accumulated for reuse.
results: Executable subagent accumulation re-executes complex tasks more reliably than textual experience.
limitations: Code subagents can be brittle across task shifts; accumulation needs curation to avoid bloat.
2603.18000.fits: Voyager's 'code-as-skill' applied to *subagents* — the library holds working programs, the strongest form of reusable experience.
2603.18000.reading: Read the subagent-as-code representation and the refine-from-feedback loop (§3–4).

2604.20133.tldr: EvoAgent: multi-file structured skills with triggers + a hierarchical sub-agent delegation loop, closed by user feedback.
2604.20133.method: Models skills as multi-file structured units with triggers and evolutionary metadata; a user-feedback-driven loop generates/optimizes skills, and three-stage matching + three-layer memory route tasks to hierarchical sub-agents.
results: Structured skill learning + delegation improves evolvability and task handling over flat skill stores.
limitations: Relies on user feedback for the closed loop; delegation hierarchy adds complexity.
2604.20133.fits: Industrializes the Voyager idea — structured (multi-file, metadata, triggers) skill units plus delegation.
2604.20133.reading: Read the skill-unit structure and the matching/delegation mechanism (§3–4).

2507.03616.tldr: EvoAgentX: an open-source platform that automates generation, execution, and optimization of agentic workflows in one framework.
2507.03616.method: Platform that automates the generation, execution, and optimization of multi-agent workflows, integrating evolution/optimization algorithms into a unified framework with native dynamic evolution.
results: Automates workflow configuration that was previously manual, with built-in dynamic evolution.
limitations: Platform-level contribution; evolved workflows are bounded by available operators.
2507.03616.fits: The tooling that operationalizes harness/workflow evolution — read when you want to *run* workflow evolution, not just read about it.
2507.03616.reading: Read the generation–execution–optimization architecture (§3) and the integrated algorithms.

2510.23601.tldr: Alita-G: a generalist agent self-evolves into a domain expert by generating, abstracting, and curating MCP tools.
2510.23601.method: A generalist agent runs a curation loop that generates, abstracts, and curates Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, transforming itself into a domain expert by accumulating reusable tools.
results: Self-generated MCP tools turn a generalist into a domain specialist, improving domain performance.
limitations: Tool quality is bounded by the generator; curation needs a feedback signal.
2510.23601.fits: Tool-creation as self-improvement — the agent extends itself by building the tools it needs (the MCP-native path).

2402.17574.tldr: Agent-Pro: evolve the agent's *behavioral policy* (beliefs and decisions), not just its prompts, for interactive games.
2402.17574.method: Learns policy-level knowledge — beliefs and decision rules — for interactive games via reflection and optimization, evolving the behavioral policy through play rather than tuning fixed prompts.
results: Improves on dynamic game scenarios (e.g., Blackjack) where prompt-only agents plateau.
limitations: Policy space is domain-specific; evaluated on small interactive games.
2402.17574.fits: Moves self-evolution from prompts to the *decision layer* — a precursor to policy-level RL agents.

2409.00872.tldr: Self-evolving Reflective Memory: combine iterative feedback, reflection, and an Ebbinghaus memory optimizer for multi-task, long-span agents.
2409.00872.method: Integrates iterative feedback, reflective mechanisms, and an Ebbinghaus-forgetting-curve memory optimizer to improve continuous decision-making across multi-task, long-span settings.
results: Enhanced multi-tasking and long-span information handling over fixed-memory baselines.
limitations: Generic framework; gains are incremental and task-dependent.
2409.00872.fits: A compact synthesis of stage-3 reflection and stage-4 memory for long-horizon agents.

2305.19118.tldr: Divergent Thinking: self-reflection alone degenerates ('degeneration of thought'); multi-agent *debate* preserves divergent, higher-quality reasoning.
2305.19118.method: Multiple LLM agents hold a debate, each proposing and challenging solutions; the paper demonstrates that single-agent self-reflection suffers from Degeneration-of-Thought while debate sustains divergence.
results: Multi-agent debate improves reasoning and mitigates the 'degeneration of thought' observed in single-agent self-reflection.
limitations: Needs multiple agents/compute; debate quality depends on agent diversity.
2305.19118.fits: The empirical argument that *other agents* — not self-feedback — are a better correction signal; motivates the multi-agent arc.
2305.19118.reading: Read the DoT analysis (§3) and the debate setup (§4).

2305.14325.tldr: Multiagent Debate: multiple model instances propose and debate their answers, iteratively converging on more factual reasoning.
2305.14325.method: Multiple LLM instances propose answers and reasoning, then iterate — each sees the others' responses and refines — converging toward a more truthful/factual answer.
results: Improves factuality (truthfulness, arithmetic, reasoning) over single-model baselines.
limitations: Compute multiplies with agents; agreement can still converge on shared errors.
2305.14325.fits: The canonical multi-agent debate — the social alternative to single-model self-correction.
2305.14325.reading: Read the debate protocol (§3) and how disagreement drives convergence.

2511.16043.tldr: Agent0: evolve agents from *zero human data* via tool-integrated reasoning and self-play RL.
2511.16043.method: Removes human-curated data: the agent self-generates a curriculum via tool-integrated reasoning and self-play RL, evolving skills (tool use, dynamic reasoning) without external supervision.
results: Evolves agents capable of tool use and dynamic reasoning from zero human data.
limitations: Self-generated curricula risk low-quality or degenerate signals; heavy compute.
2511.16043.fits: The 'zero human data' extreme of self-evolution, pairing with the multi-agent self-play lineage.
2511.16043.reading: Read the curriculum generation + tool-integrated reasoning (§3–4).

2406.14228.tldr: EvoAgent (multi-agent): automatically generate specialized multi-agent teams via evolutionary algorithms, instead of hand-designing them.
2406.14228.method: Evolutionary algorithm over agent designs: generate, select, and mutate specialized multi-agent teams so expert roles emerge automatically.
results: Auto-generated multi-agent systems match/beat human-designed frameworks on several tasks.
limitations: EA over agent populations is LLM-call expensive; specialist roles can overfit tasks.
2406.14228.fits: Applies ADAS-style search to *multi-agent teams* — the meta-agent now composes societies, not just single agents.

2403.08715.tldr: SOTOPIA-π: train social intelligence — behavior cloning + self-reinforcement on LLM-rated social interactions.
2403.08715.method: Interactive social learning: behavior cloning + self-reinforcement training on filtered social-interaction data, using LLM ratings to improve social goal-achievement (not just task skill).
results: A 7B model trained this way improves social goal-achievement on SOTOPIA.
limitations: Social intelligence is hard to evaluate; LLM ratings are a proxy.
2403.08715.fits: Extends self-improvement to *social* capability — the dimension multi-agent settings actually exercise.

2412.21139.tldr: SWE-Gym: the first *training environment* for software-engineering agents — 2,438 real Python tasks with runtime + tests — used to train agents and verifiers.
2412.21139.method: First training environment for SWE agents: 2,438 real-world Python task instances (codebase + executable runtime + unit tests + NL task); used to RL-train agents and inference-time verifiers.
results: Trained agents gain up to +19% absolute on SWE-Bench Verified/Lite; verifiers add inference-time scaling.
limitations: Python-only; training an agent still needs a strong base model.
2412.21139.fits: The infrastructure that turns code self-improvement from demo into trainable capability — supplies the environment DGM and self-modifying agents assume.
2412.21139.reading: Read the environment design (§3) and the training results (§4–5).

2304.05128.tldr: Self-Debug: teach the LLM to debug its own code — explain the program, then generate a fix — via few-shot demonstrations.
2304.05128.method: Few-shot demonstrations teach the LLM to debug its predicted program by explaining the code, then generating a fix; optionally uses execution results (traceback) as extra signal.
results: Large gains on code generation (e.g., up to ~12%+ on Text-to-SQL, TransCoder, MBPP) without training.
limitations: Improvement depends on the debugging demonstrations; gains vary by task.
2304.05128.fits: The code-domain instantiation of Self-Refine — self-correction applied to programs, with execution as optional ground truth.
2304.05128.reading: Read the explain-then-fix loop (§3) and the execution-feedback variant.

2312.13010.tldr: AgentCoder: split code generation into programmer + test-designer + test-executor agents that iterate against execution feedback.
2312.13010.method: Decomposes code generation into specialized agents — programmer, test designer, and test executor — that iterate: generate tests, run them, and refine code against execution feedback.
results: Improves code-generation accuracy (e.g., HumanEval/MBPP) over single-agent generation.
limitations: Multi-agent orchestration adds calls/latency; wrong tests can steer the fix astray.
2312.13010.fits: The multi-agent + execution-feedback recipe for code — the same ingredients (agents + tests + iteration) SWE agents use at scale.
2312.13010.reading: Read the three-role decomposition and iterative loop (§3).

2601.14525.tldr: Execution-Grounded AI Research: build an automated executor to implement ideas and launch parallel GPU experiments, then let the LLM learn from execution feedback.
2601.14525.method: Builds an automated executor that implements research ideas and launches large-scale parallel GPU experiments, then converts two real problems (LLM pre-training and LLM evaluation) into execution-grounded RL so the LLM learns from real execution.
results: Shows automated execution is feasible and that LLMs can learn from execution feedback on real research problems.
limitations: Scoped to two research problems; large GPU cost; 'feasible', not yet broadly general.
2601.14525.fits: The missing piece the AI Scientist v1 lacked — grounding idea generation in *actual execution*, closing the idea→experiment→feedback loop.
2601.14525.reading: Read the executor design and the two converted problems (§3–4).

2608.17906.tldr: AutoResearch: a two-stage system — Idea Generation integrates research signals into hypotheses; Idea Execution establishes them experimentally ('insight in, hallucination out').
2608.17906.method: Two stages: Idea Generation continuously integrates emerging research signals with accumulated domain knowledge to identify hypotheses; Idea Execution reliably establishes them through experimentation.
results: Grounds autonomous research workflows so ideas are experimentally established, reducing hallucinated claims.
limitations: Still narrows to ML research; idea quality depends on the signal-integration stage.
2608.17906.fits: Splits AI research into generation vs. execution and glues them — the mature form of the idea→experiment loop.
2608.17906.reading: Read the two-stage decomposition (§3) and how execution grounds ideas.

2607.28568.tldr: Frontis-MA1 / OpenMLE: an open full-stack testbed for RSI in machine-learning engineering — gym + RL + evolutionary search — training a 35B meta-evolution agent.
2607.28568.method: OpenMLE: open full-stack for RSI in MLE — verifiable task environments (Gym), operator learning (RL), long-horizon search (Evo) — on which a 35B model (Frontis-MA1) is post-trained as a meta-evolution agent.
results: Provides an executable, verifiable testbed for AI4AI/RSI in MLE, with a trained meta-evolution agent.
limitations: MLE-scoped; requires the OpenMLE stack; the 35B model is a research artifact.
2607.28568.fits: Turns 'AI improving the AI-building process' into a concrete, verifiable benchmark + agent — the RSI claim made testable.
2607.28568.reading: Read the three-layer stack (Gym/RL/Evo) and the agent post-training (§3–4).

2603.01712.tldr: FT-Dojo: an interactive benchmark for autonomous LLM fine-tuning — 13 tasks across 5 domains for end-to-end fine-tuning agents.
2603.01712.method: Interactive benchmark where an agent must curate data, configure training, and diagnose model behavior end-to-end, across 13 tasks in 5 domains.
results: Systematically studies end-to-end fine-tuning as an agent task, exposing where agents fail.
limitations: A benchmark, not a method; task coverage is still small.
2603.01712.fits: The 'fine-tuning as an agent task' testbed — the environment for the next level of self-improvement (improving training itself).
2603.01712.reading: Read the task taxonomy (§3) and the agent baselines/analysis (§5).

2606.06473.tldr: MLEvolve: self-evolving multi-agent framework for automated ML algorithm discovery, with hierarchical control and cross-branch memory.
2606.06473.method: Extends ML-engineering agents with hierarchical control, cross-branch information sharing, and persistent (non-memoryless) search to evolve end-to-end ML algorithms over long horizons.
results: Improves long-horizon ML algorithm discovery vs. prior MLE agents by removing inter-branch isolation and memoryless search.
limitations: Compute-heavy evolutionary search; gains are in MLE task settings.
2606.06473.fits: AlphaEvolve/AutoML-Zero's descendant for *ML algorithm* discovery — with the memory/control machinery to make long-horizon search work.
2606.06473.reading: Read the hierarchical-control + cross-branch memory design (§3–4).

2601.10657.tldr: PACEvolve: diagnose *why* self-evolving agents stall (context pollution, mode collapse) and fix it with progress-aware, consistency-preserving evolution.
2601.10657.method: Identifies that self-evolving agents anchor reasoning to local context; PACEvolve adds progress-aware, consistency-preserving mechanisms to keep long-horizon evolution on track.
results: Mitigates local-anchoring failure modes, improving long-horizon evolution across code optimization and discovery.
limitations: Mechanisms add complexity; evaluated on specific long-horizon domains.
2601.10657.fits: The diagnostic + fix for why self-evolving agents stall — the engineering prerequisite for truly long-horizon open-ended evolution.
2601.10657.reading: Read the failure-mode study (§2–3) and the progress-aware mechanism (§4).

openreview-higher-order-evolution-2024.tldr: Higher-order evolution: evolve the mutation rate, recursively the meta-mutation rate, up to a self-referential top-level parameter that modifies itself.
openreview-higher-order-evolution-2024.method: Evolves higher-order parameters (mutation rate → meta-mutation rate → … up to a self-referential top-level parameter that modifies itself), showing this improves robustness in Population-Based Training and Unsupervised Environment Design.
results: Self-referential mutation improves robustness to initial hyperparameters and enables complex adaptation in competitive multi-agent settings.
limitations: Small-scale domains (PBT/UED); self-referential levels are still bounded in practice.
openreview-higher-order-evolution-2024.fits: The evolutionary-computation counterpart to the Gödel Agent — the meta-parameters of evolution are themselves evolved, one step toward self-referential search.
openreview-higher-order-evolution-2024.reading: Read the higher-order/self-referential mutation definitions (§2–3) and the PBT/UED results.

1901.01753.tldr: POET: co-evolve environments and their solutions, transferring solutions between niches — an endless self-generated curriculum of stepping stones.
1901.01753.method: Co-evolves a population of environments and their specialized solutions; solutions transfer between niches, and the system continually generates more complex/diverse environments.
results: Finds solutions to problems it never directly targeted (stepping-stone transfer), including a hard-to-discover bipedal walker via indirect transfer.
limitations: Simple 2D-locomotion domains; the open-ended loop is hard to stabilize and scale.
1901.01753.fits: The canonical 'generate your own problems' system — POWERPLAY made evolutionary and open-ended; the lineage behind UED and modern self-generated curricula.
1901.01753.reading: Read the co-evolution + transfer mechanism (§3) and the stepping-stone result (§4).

agent-zero.what: A general-purpose agent framework that gives the agent a full Linux computer — a Dockerized desktop, annotated browser, document cowork, skills/plugins, and a bridge back to your host.
architecture: Dockerized Linux desktop + browser with DOM annotation for real computer/GUI control.
Projects, skills, and plugins as persistent capabilities the agent composes.
Host bridge lets the agent act on and coordinate with the user's own machine.
agent-zero.run: Docker-based: `docker compose up` (see the Quick Start in the README) launches the desktop + browser; add your LLM API key.
agent-zero.note: An 'extensible substrate' — the harness *is* a whole computer. Study it for how an OS-level workspace generalizes far beyond a chat loop.

deepseek-harness.what: DeepSeek's open-source agent harness, built on an everything-is-a-plugin architecture (powered by Cordis), with web and CLI runtimes.
architecture: Everything-is-a-plugin: tools, memory, and orchestration are all plugins composed via Cordis (spatiotemporal composability).
Web UI + CLI launch modes; developer preview with a documented safety notice.
deepseek-harness.run: `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web` starts the Web UI at http://127.0.0.1:3080 (Node.js required).
deepseek-harness.note: A production-grade harness from a frontier lab — the plugin architecture is the reusable idea (contrast with monolithic harnesses).

openclaw.what: A self-hosted personal assistant that runs on your own devices and lives in your chats (Node.js, MIT).
architecture: Runs locally across your devices rather than in a hosted cloud.
Chat-native: plugs into existing messaging surfaces as an assistant.
Distributed as `openclaw` on npm; Node.js runtime.
openclaw.run: `npm install -g openclaw` (or `npx openclaw`) then follow onboarding; Node.js required.
openclaw.note: The 'assistant on your own hardware' substrate — useful for studying how self-improvement is shaped by local, persistent execution.

pi.what: Pi's agent harness — a monorepo whose centerpiece is a self-extensible coding agent.
architecture: Monorepo packages: `pi-coding-agent` (interactive CLI), `pi-agent-core` (agent runtime with tool calling + state), `pi-ai` (unified multi-provider LLM API).
The self-extensible coding agent builds on the runtime to extend its own capabilities.
pi.note: A clean split of runtime / LLM-API / coding-agent — the layered design makes 'self-extension' concrete (the agent modifies its own tool set).

hermes-agent.what: Nous Research's Hermes agent and desktop app — a general-purpose local agent with a full desktop interface.
architecture: Agent runtime + desktop client (macOS/Windows/Linux).
MIT-licensed; docs at hermes-agent.nousresearch.com.
hermes-agent.run: Install the desktop app or run from source per the README/docs.
hermes-agent.note: A usability-focused harness — good for seeing how memory/tools surface in a real product rather than a research scaffold.

seal.what: SEAL (Self-Adapting LLMs) trains models via RL to generate *self-edits* — their own finetuning data and update directives — in response to new inputs.
architecture: RL loop where the model proposes edits (finetuning data + update directives) to itself.
Two domains: general-knowledge (absorb new facts) and few-shot (adapt to new tasks).
MIT CSAIL; code + data for both domains in the repo.
seal.run: Python; `git clone`, set up a conda/venv (README §Setup), then run the domain scripts.
seal.note: A model-level self-improvement substrate: the model writes the *data and update instructions* for its own adaptation — a concrete bridge between weight-space and data-space RSI.

letta-code.what: A stateful agent harness where agents have memory, identity, and experience — and can rewrite their own memory, skills, prompts, and the harness itself via 'mods'.
architecture: Stateful agents with persistent memory/identity/experience over long horizons.
Self-modification: agents rewrite their own memory, skills, prompts, and harness (mods).
Surfaces: CLI, desktop app, browser (chat.letta.com), and messaging channels.
letta-code.run: `npx @letta-ai/letta-code` for the CLI; desktop app available for macOS/Windows/Linux.
letta-code.note: One of the most direct 'harness that modifies itself' products — study the mods mechanism for how self-modification is scoped safely.

memento-skills.what: A skill-centric agent runtime where agents design agents — deploying reusable, persistent, extensible skills.
architecture: Skill-centric runtime: capabilities are packaged as reusable skills.
Reflection-based replanning on top of skill calls for multi-step tasks.
Desktop app (Windows/macOS) plus source build.
memento-skills.run: Desktop app (memento.run/release) or build from source per the README.
memento-skills.note: The 'skills as the unit of agent capability' substrate — compare its skill model to Voyager/AgentFactory's code-as-skill.

architecture: Infrastructure for agents that continually learn and self-improve.
Python 3.12+, Apache-2.0, published as `reef-infra` on PyPI.
reef.note: Infrastructure rather than a single agent — the plumbing (experience collection, updates, evaluation) a self-improving agent needs to run continuously.

autoresearch.what: Karpathy's experiment: hand an agent a small but real LLM-training setup and let it improve it autonomously overnight.
architecture: Agent modifies training code, trains ~5 minutes, checks whether the result improved, keeps or discards, repeats.
Built on a simplified single-GPU nanochat implementation.
Logs experiments so you wake up to a history — and hopefully a better model.
autoresearch.run: Python; single-GPU; see README for the nanochat-based setup.
autoresearch.note: A deliberately *small, real* self-improvement loop — the minimal reproducible 'AI improving its own training code'. Note: distinct from the AutoResearch *paper* (2608.17906).

evolutionary-model-merge.what: Sakana's Evolutionary Model Merge — evolve recipes for merging multiple foundation models in weight space (no training).
architecture: Evolution (CMA-ES) searches layer-wise merge ratios and permutations.
Combines several open models into one merged model with each's strengths (e.g., Japanese + math + code).
Hub for released merged models (e.g., EvoLLM-JP-v1-7B) + evaluation code.
evolutionary-model-merge.run: Python; evaluation scripts + released models on Hugging Face (SakanaAI org).
evolutionary-model-merge.note: Model-level self-improvement by *recombination* — improving an AI by evolving how existing weights are mixed, cheaper than gradient descent.

openevolve.what: An open-source evolutionary coding agent — turns an LLM into an autonomous code optimizer that discovers better algorithms.
architecture: Evolutionary loop: LLM proposes code variants, an evaluator scores them, the best survive and seed the next generation.
From random search to state-of-the-art — refines programs against a fitness signal.
Distributed as `openevolve` on PyPI with system-message guides.
openevolve.run: `pip install openevolve`; see Quick Start and Examples in the README.
openevolve.note: The 'LLM + evaluator + evolution' recipe (FunSearch/AlphaEvolve) packaged as a drop-in library — the fastest way to *run* an evolutionary coding loop.

agentfactory.what: Code for AgentFactory — self-evolution by accumulating executable subagents.
architecture: Successful solutions are saved as executable subagent code, refined by execution feedback.
The subagent library is reused as composable building blocks for new tasks.
agentfactory.run: Python; set an LLM API key and run the agent-factory loop (see README).
agentfactory.note: Run it after reading the paper to see 'code-as-skill' concretely — watch how subagents accumulate and get refined.

dgm.what: The Darwin Gödel Machine — the self-modifying coding agent with archive-based evolution.
architecture: The agent edits its own source code; only empirically-validated edits are kept.
A MAP-Elites-style archive stores and evolves past improvements open-endedly.
dgm.run: Python; provide an LLM API key; the agent runs its edit → evaluate → keep loop on a task (see README).
dgm.note: The flagship self-modifier — run it to watch the improver-improves-the-improver loop on real code.

godel-agent.what: Gödel Agent — a self-referential agent whose behavior is code it can inspect and rewrite.
architecture: Prompts + tools form the agent's 'code', which it can read and modify.
Self-modification loop with heuristic validation.
godel-agent.run: Python; LLM API key; run the self-modification loop per README.
godel-agent.note: The theory-side companion to DGM — run it to see self-reference as code-as-identity in practice.

hyperagents.what: HyperAgents — self-improvement where the meta-level (the improver) is itself improvable code.
architecture: Meta-level and object-level are both coding tasks, so both are editable.
Builds on DGM: the improvement mechanism is itself coded and improvable.
hyperagents.run: Python (Meta); LLM API key; see README for the hyperagent loop.
hyperagents.note: Read DGM first, then run this to see the meta-level made explicit and improvable.

sia.what: SIA — Self Improving AI with joint harness + weight updates.
architecture: A Feedback-Agent updates both the harness and the task agent's weights.
Unifies the harness-update and test-time-training schools.
sia.run: Python; LLM API key + training setup; run the Feedback-Agent loop per README.
sia.note: The 'close the loop' system — study how harness edits and weight updates are coordinated in one feedback agent.

ace.what: ACE — Agentic Context Engineering; evolves the whole context as a playbook.
architecture: Context as an evolving playbook: generation, reflection, curation.
Structured incremental edits avoid context collapse.
ace.run: Python; LLM API key; run the context-evolution loop per README.
ace.note: Watch how the *whole context* evolves (vs. Voyager's code skills) — prompt-space self-improvement.

architecture: Meta-learning over the memory design (what to store, update, retrieve).
Memory adapts to task diversity and non-stationarity instead of being fixed.
alma.note: Run to see memory *architecture* learned rather than hand-crafted — the meta level over memory.

continual-harness.what: Continual Harness — reset-free online self-improvement (the Gemini Plays Pokémon lineage).
architecture: The agent alternates acting and refining its prompt, sub-agents, skills, and memory.
Single continuous trajectory, no resets.
continual-harness.run: Python; embodied/Pokémon environment + LLM API; see README.
continual-harness.note: Run if you want the reset-free, embodied flavor of harness self-improvement.

evoagentx.what: EvoAgentX — a platform to generate, execute, and optimize agentic workflows.
architecture: Automates workflow generation + execution + optimization.
Integrates evolution/optimization algorithms in one unified framework.
evoagentx.note: The tooling for *running* workflow evolution — pair with the paper to see the search algorithms concretely.

evolver.what: EvolveR — self-evolving agents via an experience-driven lifecycle.
architecture: Trajectories are distilled into abstract strategic principles.
Offline distillation + online retrieval + outcome-reinforced policy.
evolver.run: Python; LLM API key; run the lifecycle loop per README.
evolver.note: The end-to-end 'experience → principle → policy' loop — run to see *strategy* (not fact) memory.

voyager.what: Voyager — an open-ended embodied agent that builds a growing skill library in Minecraft.
architecture: An automatic curriculum proposes tasks; execution-verified code skills accumulate in a library.
Environment feedback refines skills; later tasks reuse earlier skills.
voyager.run: Python; needs Minecraft + MineDojo and an OpenAI API key; entry point `voyage.py`.
voyager.note: The canonical skill-library agent — run it (if you have Minecraft) to watch skills compound.

adas.what: ADAS (Automated Design of Agentic Systems) — a meta-agent that programs new agents.
architecture: A meta-agent proposes agent designs as executable code and evaluates them.
A re-architect step improves the meta-agent's own prompt.
adas.run: Python; LLM API key; run the meta-agent search per README.
adas.note: The harness-level flagship — run to see an improver that *generates executable improvements*.

ai-scientist.what: The AI Scientist — an end-to-end ML research loop (idea → experiment → paper → review).
architecture: Idea generation (novelty-checked) → experiments → plots → LaTeX paper → automated reviewer.
Iterates; on the order of ~$15 per paper.
ai-scientist.run: Python; LLM API keys; run the pipeline over a research template (see README).
ai-scientist.note: Run it to see 'AI doing AI research' end to end; read v2 for the agentic-search upgrade.

funsearch.what: FunSearch — LLM + evaluator + evolution that discovered new mathematics (cap sets).
architecture: A frozen LLM proposes candidate functions in a problem skeleton; an evaluator scores them.
The best functions are fed back as few-shot examples (an evolutionary loop).
funsearch.run: Python (Jupyter); provides the evaluator + program-sampler framework.
funsearch.note: The cleanest 'LLM + evaluator' loop — study the evaluate → select → prompt cycle, then run a toy problem.

mlevolve.what: MLEvolve — a self-evolving multi-agent framework for automated ML algorithm discovery.
architecture: Hierarchical control + cross-branch memory + persistent search.
Evolves end-to-end ML algorithms over long horizons.
mlevolve.run: Python; LLM API key; run the evolutionary search per README.
mlevolve.note: AlphaEvolve's descendant for *ML algorithm* discovery — run to see long-horizon evolutionary search.

poet.what: POET (Paired Open-Ended Trailblazer) — co-evolves environments and their solutions.
architecture: Co-evolves a population of environments and their specialized solutions; transfers between niches.
Endlessly generates harder, more diverse environments.
poet.note: The canonical 'generate your own problems' system — run the classic to see open-ended curricula in miniature.

2609.20519.tldr: Runs auto-research loops over the coding-agent harness itself under a token-efficiency objective: 152 proposed mechanisms, four survive — ~45% fewer tokens and ~1/3 lower cost while retaining ~94% of Pi's score.
2609.20519.method: A 7-stage auto-research loop per candidate idea: Trajectory Rollouts -> Map-Reduce Analysis -> Proposal -> Implementation -> Reviewer -> In-Trajectory Validation -> Held-Out Validation on a frozen, isolated test set. A predeclared capability floor gates every mechanism (savings only count within a quality tolerance, so efficiency is bounded by non-regression), and the surviving mechanisms combine into the SoL-Pi harness.
results: 44.7-49% fewer recorded tokens and ~1/3 lower API cost vs Pi, retaining ~94% of Pi's EdgeBench score (and exceeding the native Codex harness on GPT-5.6 Sol).

Four reusable mechanisms: Action Fusion (fuse edit+run into one call), Online Context Compact (compact at subtask boundaries), ObservationPack (paged recall instead of full replay), Evidence-Preserving Reducer (delegate first reading to a cheaper agent, verify against the log).
In a 20-worker swarm, SoL-Pi workers reach 1,127 cycles at $60.11 — 17.5% fewer cycles and 26.8% lower cost than Pi workers.
limitations: Efficiency measured against Pi and model-native harnesses on EdgeBench/Terminal-Bench; cross-harness transferability is claimed via held-out environments, not yet proven at scale.
Hybrid loop: human priors seeded and filtered the 152-idea pool, so it is not fully autonomous RSI.
The recursive-efficiency compounding ('REI') is explicitly a vision, not a demonstrated effect.
2609.20519.fits: Harness-level RSI with an efficiency objective gated by a capability floor — the non-regression discipline rsif encodes as its val gate, now applied to token cost. Complements rsif (which evolves the agent's artifacts) by evolving the harness that runs the agent.
2609.20519.reading: Read the 7-stage loop and the predeclared capability floor / gate; the four mechanism cards show how narrow harness edits transfer across tasks.
